ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are three relatively long blue horizontal line segments, and on each line there is the same pink arrow mark, indicating that these three horizontal lines are parallel to one another. On the right side there is a blue slanted line that intersects the middle horizontal line and the bottom horizontal line in sequence; near the middle intersection point is marked the angle (4x−5)°, and near the bottom intersection point, in the corresponding position, is marked the angle (3x+11)°. Reasoning: Because the middle horizontal line and the bottom horizontal line are parallel, and the slanted line on the right is a transversal, these two corresponding angles are equal. Set up the equation: 4x−5 = 3x+11. Subtract 3x from both sides to get x−5 = 11; add 5 to both sides to get x = 16.
